statement: For k<n, generic unrestricted complementary affine sections of St(k,n) have geometric monodromy S_D, where D is the matrix-entry degree.

answer.text: For k<n, generic unrestricted complementary affine sections of St(k,n) have geometric monodromy S_D, where D is the matrix-entry degree.
answer.display: For k<n: S_D, D=deg St(k,n). The k=n orthogonal case is excluded here.

source.location: Proposition 1.1 (PDF p.1); Remark 3.4 (PDF p.8); explicit Bertini reduction in caveats
source.version: arXiv:1809.07293v2 (24 October 2018). Proposition 1.1 and its proof apply in characteristic zero. The 2023 corrigendum concerns a characteristic-seven trinomial and does not affect this application.

notes:
This is an explicitly deduced consequence, not a claim that Kadets discusses this named variety. Take a general codimension dim(V)−1 linear section of the irreducible projective closure V. Bertini gives an integral curve C of degree D. Proposition 1.1 gives S_D as C meets a variable hyperplane; these loops are a subfamily of the unrestricted complementary-section problem, so the ambient monodromy contains S_D and equals S_D. For affine sections, a general complementary section misses the boundary V at infinity, which has dimension dim(V)−1; restricting the unramified base to this nonempty open preserves monodromy. This argument does not apply to fixed coordinate projections, physically constrained measurement subfamilies or reducible varieties. This fills only k<n. At k=n the variety is O(n), with two components; the full symmetric-group argument is inapplicable. Irreducibility and smoothness for k<n are proved in Brysiewicz–Gesmundo, arXiv:1909.10085v2, Lemma 2.4; degree in Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 4.2, https://arxiv.org/html/1909.10085v2 .
